description: Multi-phase plans currently in flight. Each phase references roadmap item ids; the activePhase section breaks the current phase into concrete tasks with status. Survives conversation compactions — a fresh session can pick up by reading this file.

Momus reviewed the build (holes fixed in 71fbe28; fixed version not re-reviewed) and the temple-codex run (0 contradicted). phases.notes: Theseus was the most-used agent in cass-vessel (~50 reports, ~1MB, Dec 24 - Feb 23) but reports pile up unindexed. Tasks: report index with open/done per monster; link resolved monsters to decisions/gameplan resolutions; prune or archive stale reports; gitignore editor lock files (a .~lock.battle-plan.md# got committed in cass-vessel).

phases.title: Evidence: resume benchmark vs plain Claude Code
phases.notes: Wonderland lesson: its $30.58 / 63% claim compared only against its own earlier version, and its own analysis 046 puts overhead at ~10x single-shot ($2-3). Tasks: pre-register falsifier with Momus before running; build handoff scenarios (half-finished task + prior decisions); score fresh session with vs without Daedalus memory on correct next step and decision adherence; port per-run cost telemetry (wonderland-ai src/wonderland/telemetry.py) so every claim carries cost; reuse comparison-baseline harness ideas (paper/artifacts/comparison-baselines/). Put the number, with its caveats, in the README.

phases.title: Workstreams: concurrent plans, collisions, per-owner drift
phases.notes: DONE 2026-10-13: PR #26 merged (915d65d), Momus-reviewed (follow-ups in 7b832e7, incl. a dated-window fix for reconstruct). Edict 0008. Build after PR #22 (0006) merges: both touch the gameplan code. Its first test reproduces 2026-10-13 (Ariadne + memory sessions both active). Open design points: owner identity (git author pattern vs session), migration is a no-op (existing gameplan = default workstream).

phases.title: Agent board: threads between owners' agents over a git branch
phases.notes: RESHAPED 2026-10-13: 0009 amended into a message board (Kohl). Threads readable by the whole team instead of point-to-point inboxes: one answer serves every agent; threads hang off edicts, workstreams, or file paths; collisions get negotiated in the open. Keeps 0009's git transport, hooks, owner-approved posts and citation checks; needs follow/filter to control noise (e.g. threads touching your workstream's claims). Edict 0009. Depends on p5 (0008). OPTION TO EXPLORE (not in the edict): near-real-time delivery to an open but idle session via an async SessionStart hook with asyncRewake (hook settings schema: runs in background, wakes the model on exit 2) polling the mail branch. Untested; prove it in a spike before relying on it. Same rules apply: inbound mail is data, replies need owner approval. Also later, if latency matters: a relay server (e.g. MCP) carrying the same message format.

CIRCLE BACK: after the TUI build, decide on a separate edict making Ophanic part of Daedalus (notation skill + width checker, opt-in; not the ophanic parser, which is unreliable as of 2026-10-14). activePhase.title: Accepted edicts + Ariadne verification gaps
activePhase.goal: Build the three accepted edicts to their acceptance criteria and close the verifier gaps that let LLM-only review pass broken code.
activePhase.sequencing: p1 is being worked by a parallel session (Ariadne: T-e5, T-e8..T-e11). Non-Ariadne tasks: T-e7 (0005 opt-in) and the edict list/show CLI half of T-e1; the T-e1 intent gate lives in the orchestrator, so coordinate before touching it. T-e1's edict CLI is shared infrastructure for T-e2 and T-e7. T-e3 is independent. T-e4 is high value (reviewers approved code that failed at import). T-e6 is small housekeeping. Edict 0006 (p2b) is being built in parallel on feat/0006-reconstruction; it is not the active phase because activating it would clear p1's tasks.

tasks.title: Edict 0001: intent flows from edicts
tasks.details: _diff_intent() stops falling back to diff.description; missing metadata['intent'] -> NEEDS_REVIEW in every autonomy mode; daedalus edict list|show; status -> done when all tagged diffs merge; tests for fail-closed, edict-sourced intent, transitions. NOTE: 0001's header reads 'Status: acccepted' (typo). A strict parser treats it as not accepted; Kohl must fix it (Daedalus may not edit edicts).
tasks.resolution: 0001 approved-intent gate (as amended: edict or approved plan; never from metadata), edict list/show. PR #23+#24 merged in 915d65d; Momus-reviewed, holes fixed in 4f8e892.

tasks.title: Edict 0003: dissent
tasks.details: daedalus edict dissent <id> / edict dissents; open dissent blocks dispatch; judge may cite open dissent for NEEDS_HUMAN; history never deleted. Depends on T-e1's edict CLI.
tasks.resolution: 0003 dissent: edict dissent/dissents/resolve-dissent, blocks dispatch and intent, ask rule. PR #24 merged in 915d65d.

tasks.title: Edict 0002: model casting
tasks.details: worker_model / judge_model config (None = SDK default, behavior unchanged); passed to LLMJudge and ClaudeAgentOptions; recorded on diff; shown in ariadne review show. One model per role, Claude Agent SDK only.
tasks.resolution: 0002 model casting: ariadne.worker_model/judge_model through to ClaudeAgentOptions, recorded on diffs and reviews. PR #25 merged in 915d65d; shown against a stubbed SDK only (real SDK untested).

tasks.title: #15 verifier fails closed; add import/build check
tasks.details: Verifier must not pass a diff when no tests match. Add an execution check (import/compile the touched modules, cf. wonderland verify_imports / verification.py) so LLM review is never the only gate.
tasks.resolution: Phase 0 hygiene PR (2026-10-14): no matching test -> not verified (no_tests_matched); if all else passed, routed to NEEDS_REVIEW (reviewer 'verifier') instead of merged. Changed .py files are compiled first; changed test files always run. Issue #15 can close on merge.

tasks.title: #16 local worker/judge backends + live tier
tasks.details: BLOCKED: needs its own edict (0002's amendment narrowed the non-goal but does not authorize the build). Then: local backend with stub-server test, then live tier, local first on the home GPU. Guardrail: never run live model calls on an employer's account or machine.

tasks.title: Housekeeping bugs #13, #14
tasks.details: #13 permissions project-root check uses string prefix (sibling dirs count as inside) -> use Path.is_relative_to. #14 buses default to machine-wide /tmp paths -> per-project roots.

tasks.title: Edict 0005: edicts opt-in
tasks.details: edicts.enabled config (default false); init --edicts scaffolds docs/edicts/README.md + dissents/; template Edicts section conditional, with upgrade hint instead of silent drop; with edicts off every Ariadne diff routes to NEEDS_REVIEW; set edicts.enabled=true in this repo.
tasks.resolution: 0005 edicts opt-in (edicts.enabled, init --edicts, conditional template). PR #23 merged in 915d65d; its edicts-off criterion delivered by #24.

tasks.title: Harness: __pycache__ binaries end up in Ariadne diffs
tasks.details: submit_diff_to_ariadne stages with 'git add -A'; a worker that runs pytest leaves __pycache__/*.pyc in the worktree; without a .gitignore covering them the diff carries binary patches, git apply refuses them, and the verifier rejects every diff. Found by the local gate experiment (2026-10-13); hermetic tier never runs pytest in the worker so it missed this. Fix: exclude untracked ignored-by-convention artifacts (or pass PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE / stage with a default exclude list).
tasks.resolution: Phase 0 hygiene PR (2026-10-14): submit_diff_to_ariadne stages with exclude pathspecs for __pycache__, *.pyc/*.pyo and .pytest_cache; test in test_ariadne_worker_loop.py.

tasks.title: Harness: judge sees only the first line of the work package
tasks.details: execute_work_package sets the diff description to the first line of work.description and sets no metadata['intent']; the orchestrator's _diff_intent falls back to description, so for dispatcher-built packages the judge's intent is '# Task: Implement <dir> changes'. Seen live: judge approved two packages on that intent. Fix: put the full package description (and the feature's requirements) in diff.metadata['intent'].
tasks.resolution: Folded into 0001: the full work package travels to diff metadata and the judge prompt. PR #24 merged in 915d65d.

tasks.title: Planner drops requirements and inter-package dependencies
tasks.details: Planner._generate_work_packages makes one package per parent directory with description 'Modify {files} for {title}': the feature description never reaches workers. Only dependency it knows: tests depend on all impl packages; e.g. orders (needs pricing.apply_discount) runs in parallel with pricing. Kohl (2026-10-13): 'we're gonna have to spruce that up'. Evidence pending: gate experiment conditions ariadne vs ariadne+req vs local LLM planner (scratchpad gate_exp/, results to be committed).

tasks.title: Ariadne as a CLI loop: local plan -> main-agent approval -> local dispatch
tasks.details: Direction agreed with Kohl 2026-10-13 (pending experiment results). The main Claude Code session calls 'daedalus ariadne plan' (local LLM planner prints the plan into context), approves/edits it in one turn, then 'daedalus ariadne dispatch' runs local workers + gate + local judge with no claude_agent_sdk calls; the main agent reads a summary and handles NEEDS_REVIEW. Why: measured 2026-10-13, any fresh Claude subagent costs ~45-50k tokens of fixed overhead (Claude solo implemented each 7-file test feature correctly for ~47-51k; a subagent plan review cost ~49-55k), so Claude's marginal cost must stay in the main context; also removes SDK billing from the loop. Plan quality: small planners follow required schema fields (tests: file/must_cover/existing_tests_to_update) far better than prose rules. Depends on T-e5 (local backends) and T-e10 (planner). Evidence: scratchpad gate_exp/ results, to be committed with the write-up.

tasks.title: Ariadne test backlog: adversarial/scope, conflicts, sequential drift, dogfooding
tasks.details: Agreed with Kohl 2026-10-13, after mutation testing (queued; experiments/ariadne-local on exp/ariadne-local). (1) Adversarial/scope: plant diffs that weaken/delete tests, touch files outside the package, or do the task plus an unrelated change; the verifier passes all of these by design, so measure the judge plus an 'only the package's files changed' check (proposed in #16, unbuilt). (2) Conflicts: deliberately send two packages at overlapping code (same function, different intents); check the conflict detector escalates correctly instead of blocking everything. (3) Sequential drift: 10 features in a row on one codebase, each from the last one's HEAD; does main stay green, do slipped mistakes compound. (4) Dogfooding: use the CLI loop (T-e11) on real daedalus work for 1-2 weeks; track landed, reverted, bugs found later. Also analyse wall-clock and NEEDS_REVIEW queue size, already recorded per run.

tasks.title: Harness: load_icarus_identity silently falls back to a 266-char stub
tasks.details: load_icarus_identity() reads daedalus.identity.data.agents/icarus.md, which hasn't existed since c2fb6b2 moved agents into .claude-plugin/agents/; the bare except returns a minimal 'You are Icarus...' stub, so every real worker since then ran without the Icarus identity. Found 2026-10-13 building pilot arm A (H4: does identity help small models). Fix: load from the real location (or ship icarus.md as package data), and make a missing identity an error or a loud warning, not a silent fallback; add a test that the loaded identity is the full one.
tasks.resolution: PR #34 (merged 2026-10-14), shipped in 0.2.0: the identity ships as identity data (identity/data/agents/icarus.md), frontmatter stripped with an anchored match, a missing identity warns, and a sync test keeps it identical to .claude-plugin/agents/icarus.md. Kept out of plugin/agents/ so hydrate doesn't install an icarus subagent everywhere (Kohl's call if wanted). Verified from PyPI: 3507-char identity loads.

tasks.title: Orchestrator: escalated conflicts are never recorded, so incompatible diffs merge
tasks.details: Found 2026-10-13 by the colliding-pair test (pilot design). process_pending Phase 2 runs ConflictDetector.analyze_all and, for ESCALATE, does nothing; the analyses are never saved to the bus, so Phase 3's 'unresolved = bus.list_conflicts(resolved=False)' is always empty and the commit proceeds. Repro with a stub judge (experiments/ariadne-local/gate_exp/repro_conflict_escalation.py): two diffs with incompatible intents on DIFFERENT lines (add() starts rejecting negatives; new sum_all() relies on add() with negatives) -> detected=1, stored=0, both merged in one commit. Same-line conflicts only 'escape' because the combined patch fails to apply. Still present on PR #24's branch. Fix: persist escalated conflicts on the bus (or hold the conflicting diffs out of the commit batch) and test that a detected-and-escalated pair never commits.
tasks.notes: Fix in PR #28 (by daedalus-42, at Kohl's request).
tasks.resolution: Fixed by daedalus-42 in PR #28 (merged 2026-10-14): escalated conflicts are recorded on the bus and both diffs held out of the commit; unrelated diffs still land. Verified independently by Daedalus (the Ariadne experiment session): tests/test_conflict_escalation.py fails 4/4 on the pre-fix base and passes 4/4 on the fix, and the full suite passed (284). Repro: experiments/ariadne-local/gate_exp/repro_conflict_escalation.py. The colliding-pair experiment runs are pinned to the pre-fix snapshot, so they're 'before' data.

tasks.title: Greenfield experiment: local Ariadne builds the shape, Claude polishes
tasks.details: Kohl's idea 2026-10-13. Specs units and kvstore with hidden oracles (validated), in experiments/ariadne-local/greenfield/. Local conditions gf_single and gf_llmplan queue behind the overnight runs and keep every final tree as an artifact. Claude conditions staged for 2026-10-23 (greenfield/RUNBOOK.md): Claude solo; Claude polishing a local artifact; Claude writing the plan plus acceptance tests, then local build, then polish. Design point: on greenfield the planner's acceptance tests are what keep the verifier meaningful; otherwise workers grade their own tests. Metrics: oracle pass, Claude tokens, blind quality review.

tasks.title: Memory staleness and coverage heuristics (a status header with the memory)
tasks.details: Kohl's idea 2026-10-13: the model should know how current and how complete its memory is. A first pass on this repo's .daedalus/: project-map.md's content dates from 2025-12-24 with 51 commits to src/ and .claude-plugin/ since; decisions, lessons and warnings carry no date at all; project-map misses the cli package and the gameplan and momus agents (package-level coverage is too coarse to catch doctor.py or reconstruct.py); path refs are tree diagrams, so dead-reference checks must parse trees. Proposal: a date per memory section, a covers: list per section (commits-since scoped to it), module-level coverage, dead references, and a short deterministic status header shown above memory whenever it's loaded (e.g. extend 'daedalus doctor' from 0007, or add 'daedalus memory status'). Memory-workstream territory, probably an edict. Experiment hook: a third mature arm with memory plus the status header, against memory alone and none (the memory arm is queued on exp/ariadne-local).

tasks.title: Wire the Mind Palace into Ariadne: test selection, planner retrieval, causal conflicts
tasks.details: Kohl 2026-10-13: the palace goes unused but could arbitrate complex pathways through the code. Ariadne was designed for it and never wired it: extract_causal_chain's docstring says the full version integrates palace pathfinding, and ConflictDetector takes a palace_path the orchestrator never passes. Probe on the ad1675c snapshot: CallGraph.from_project builds 718 nodes (170 test functions) in 0.3 s; ImpactAnalysis links submit_diff_to_ariadne to test_ariadne_worker_loop, which name matching misses; but it finds 0 tests for _passes_semantic_review, LLMJudge.review and set_nested_value, which are tested. The static graph misses instance, self.method and injected calls. Order: (1) verifier test selection = impact analysis + names, with a full-suite fallback (pairs with T-e4/#15); (2) planner retrieval and package order from callers and callees; (3) causal-level conflicts; (4) palace staleness (build commit, drifted rooms) in the T-e16 status header. First raise graph recall: resolve self.method within the class, obj.method by unique name. Measurable offline: re-verify the mature run's stored diffs with palace-selected tests.

tasks.title: Palace query CLI for the main agent (callers, impact --tests, path, tests-for)
tasks.details: Kohl 2026-10-13: the palace should be usable by the main agent too. Today the main agent's only real route is the labyrinth subagent, at roughly 45-50k tokens of fixed overhead per spawn (measured 2026-10-13), so in practice it greps; 'daedalus palace' has only init and status. Add fast deterministic CLI queries: callers/callees <symbol>, impact <symbol> --tests, path <a> <b>, tests-for <file|diff> (full-suite fallback when nothing is found). The graph builds in 0.3 s, so rebuild or cache by HEAD. Then a Reach for Your Tools row and a mind-palace skill that uses the CLI instead of the subagent. Design rule: Daedalus capabilities the main agent should use often are CLI commands, and subagents are for long, context-heavy jobs. Shares the graph-recall work with T-e17.
tasks.resolution: PR #33 (merged 2026-10-14), shipped in 0.2.0: daedalus palace callers|callees|impact [--tests]|path|tests-for [--diff], read-only, built from source in ~0.3 s. Against coverage ground truth over 8 symbols: lists 118/127 executing tests (the palace builder's graph: 37/127); a superset (88 of 206 listings extra, concentrated in interface methods); production callers never link to test doubles. Momus-reviewed, with fixes. Graph-recall work shared with T-e17, which stays open for the verifier, planner and conflict detector integration.

tasks.title: Ariadne package contracts, ported from Wonderland
tasks.details: Multi-file features fail locally (toy features 1/45 pass, unaudited). Port Wonderland's answers into Ariadne's planner instead of designing fresh: versioned contract at each package seam that every implementation must name (wonderland contract_note.py, implementation.py); an upfront conventions charter plus shared primitives handed to every worker and checked in review (807c233); cross-package duplicate/scope-leak detection (cross_feature.py, scope_leak.py); red tests before code. Constraint (Kohl, 2026-10-14): shape the package and contract format so Ariadne can later slot into Wonderland as a component, e.g. reuse Wonderland's ticket/contract artifact shapes, not Ariadne-only ones. Not now; first audit the 0/0 runs (suspect: tests run under the wrong interpreter, see wonderland 03a1836 and verification.pytest_collects).

tasks.title: Palace beyond Python: tree-sitter frontend
tasks.details: Kohl 2026-10-14: the palace is Python-only; add a tree-sitter frontend. Grammar delivery (Kohl): both, per-language wheels by default (daedalus[palace]) and tree-sitter-language-pack when installed. Scope: element extraction, call graph, spans and tests-for, so the palace CLI queries work on JS/TS, Go, Rust, Java, C#, C/C++, Ruby (+ Kotlin/PHP/Scala/Lua via the pack). Constraint (daedalus-d9): Python query results must not change; d9's coverage measurement (118/127) quotes them. Follow-ups: T-e21, T-e22, T-e23.

tasks.title: Palace builder: non-Python module discovery
tasks.details: Cartographer still assumes Python for package/module discovery: __init__.py anchors and docstrings, analyze_python_file bypassing the registry, *.py globs, def/class module anchors, dunder skips (theseus inventory 2026-10-14: cartographer.py:180-251, 279, 371, 438-443, 634). The query CLI is language-aware after T-e20; palace rooms are not yet.

tasks.title: Ariadne verification: language-aware test selection and runner
tasks.details: ariadne/verification.py maps .py paths to modules, globs test_*.py, and runs pytest; it never calls the palace. Wire it to query.tests_reaching/convention_tests (language-aware since T-e20) and pick the test runner per language (pytest, go test, cargo test, jest/vitest, ...). causal_slice.py's dataclass/def pattern extraction and indentation block ends should move to element spans.

tasks.title: Palace: import-aware call resolution
tasks.details: Calls resolve by name only (same module, else every same-named definition up to a cap), so interface-heavy code over-links: snapd's Lock() reaches 2,667 callers. Resolving through imports (Python imports, TS paths and index files, Go packages) is the precision fix, per language. Measure against coverage ground truth as T-e18 did before and after.

tasks.title: Palace: type-informed dispatch for calls through fields and variables
tasks.details: T-e23 resolves calls bound by imports (from x import f; mod.f(); pkg.F(); Foo.bar()). Calls through a field or variable (self.reviewer.review(), s.mu.Lock(), store.save()) still use the name-based rule, so interface-heavy code over-links: snapd's Lock() keeps ~2,666 callers. Fix with light type information: constructor assignments (self.x = Foo(...), x := Foo{}), annotated parameters and fields (reviewer: LLMJudge, mu sync.Mutex), Go struct field types. Measure with the T-e18 harness (experiments/palace-recall/measure.sh on exp/ariadne-local). Note from the T-e23 measurement: on this repo the remaining extras are mostly path-sensitivity (ConflictDetector.analyze_all has one definition) and injected fakes (LLMJudge.review), which types won't fix either. daedalus-d9 (2026-10-14): this feeds test selection, where extras cost time but misses cost safety; never drop a test today's name-based link finds unless the type information is certain. Guard the recall column.

tasks.title: .NET: C#, Razor/Blazor, Unity in the palace and Ariadne
tasks.details: Kohl 2026-10-14: .NET is an important target. Scope (Kohl): C# only; ASP.NET Core APIs, Blazor/Razor, libraries/services, Unity; xUnit; dotnet build gate on by default.

tasks.title: Palace: dispatch edges from publish sites to handlers (MediatR, Hangfire, Celery, in-house queues)
tasks.details: Issue #47 (Kohl, 2026-10-15): the call graph stops at framework dispatch, so handlers show 0 callers and impact --tests misses everything upstream of a queue. Built-in rules for MediatR/MassTransit/NServiceBus (message type -> handler), Hangfire (lambda targets), Celery (task.delay -> @task); in-house rules from palace.dispatch config. Dispatch edges are labelled in callers/path/impact output. Stacked on #44 (receiver types).

tasks.title: doctor/source list: detect a stale or foreign install (old 'daedalus' dist, missing entry points)
tasks.details: On Kohl's machine the live install is a Dec 2025 user-site editable named 'daedalus' 0.1.0: deps never refreshed (tree-sitter, keyring) and no daedalus.sources entry points, so 'source list' shows no plugins. doctor's install check looks up 'daedalus-cli' and misses it. source list should say why it found no plugins. Fix for Kohl: pip uninstall --break-system-packages daedalus; pipx install --force --editable .

tasks.title: Hook registration: several Daedalus commands per event
tasks.details: hooks.py wanted_hooks/ALL_HOOKS are {event: command}, so only one Daedalus hook per event fits (board already holds UserPromptSubmit). Restructure to [(event, command, config key)], register/remove per command, hydrate --dry-run lists each. Blocks 0014's clock hook (Momus 0014 readiness F5).
tasks.resolution: PR #53 (merged 28ad709): HOOKS is a list of (event, command, hooks.* key); Momus: merge.
